Cliff's 5th place was most noteworthy for he seemed to have greater difficulty with the conditions than anyone----conditions that caused several retirements including Kerr, Bradley and O'Hara; although the latter went off course when in the first six.

Several times he appeared to be dropped and struggling while Alan Black towed O'Hara round the first 3 laps. After all, how is this for a depleted ten? - Black, Brown, Barrow, Kerr, O'Hara, Newell, Bicourt, Thorpe, Moore and Walker. It would be an even greater feat to win both trophies!
Seniors:North 3rd,North 15th,Hart 23rd,Fairclough 24th,Dabbs 29th,O'Hara 51st. Juniors:Bicourt 23rd,Cocks 51st,Hampshire 53rd,Morrison 119th---Belgrave 7th.
Alan Morrison helped our score along with a now regular sub 2 mins "half" (1:59.3) finishing second and O'Hara and Thorpe took first two places in the mile with 4:16 and 4:19:7.
However, fine packing gave BELGRAVE the team race, our four scorers being 3rd Kerr 9:12, 4th O'Hara 9:15, 6th Gerry North 9:20, 8th Hart 9:29.

Belgrave won the 2 miles team race with John Thresher the winner in 9:09 supported by Gerry North (9:20) and John Bicourt (9:28). Kerr and O'Hara took the 'A' and 'B' miles with 4:20:0 and 4:20:4 respectively.
SURREY: Gerry North, Thresher, Fairclough, Steer, Dabbs, Black. MIDDLESEX: Hart, O'Hara, Kerr, Newell, Dear and Crookes. What a pity that Geoff North, Thorpe, Barrow and Brown qualify for neither!

Our spies tell us that a certain dark-horse Irishman is amongst us showing all the signs for beating the "book"---and his name is not O'Hara either!
SHORT STAGES: Geoff North, O'Hara, Williams, Bicourt, Dance, Major,. With Black, Dabbs, Steer, Buxton, Dear and a host of others itching to get in, the lads should really be on their Mettle.
Major issues in the middle distance such as O'HARA, BUXTON And KERR have slipped a few seconds whilst NORTH industries are experiencing injuries and do not at present inspire a buyers market.
The team that eventually took part was but a shadow of our full strength with names such as Fairclough, Hart, O'Hara, Steer, Thresher and Whewell missing from the line up.

I wonder what Thresher, Fairclough, Major, Bicourt, O'Hara, Hart, Dabbs, Steer etc. think of that. Agreed that the North brothers, Dance, Whewell, Williams, Kerr and others have played parts of varying degrees in our success but they joined us on moving to London because they had to change their club.
For the short legs Hart, O'Connor, Dance and Diprose look well placed, with the last two places to be scrambled for by Bicourt, O'Hara, Piotrowski, Cross and Kerr.
On his left is the link man Major the ex-minor who is making a name for himself in the big time. Then there is Scarlet O'Hara and Doug Brew - Doug Brew - I ask you!

Bill Dance is keeping in fine trim up in Huddersfield, and Major and O'Hara are also running into form again. Last, but by no means least, we have that ever-present spearhead Gerry North and the reliable Trevor Hart.
With our Surrey men nicely tuned up after Woking they will be joined by our other big guns, Mann, O'Hara and O'Connor for the Blackheath Relay seven days later.
